governance.text: s.125.0104(4)(e) F.S.: the county governing board appoints a 9-member Tourist Development Council established by ordinance: the county commission chair (or a commissioner the chair designates); two elected municipal officials, at least one from the most populous municipality in the taxing district; six people involved in the tourist industry, of whom 3 to 4 must be owners/operators of tourist accommodations subject to the tax. All members must be county electors; staggered 4-year terms; meets at least quarterly; recommends uses of revenue and continuously reviews expenditures. The council is advisory; the Board of County Commissioners adopts the budget.

governance.item: Bay County TDC as described by Visit PCB
governance.text: Nine members appointed by the Bay County Board of County Commissioners: three tax collectors, three representatives of tourist-related businesses and three elected officials. The TDC contracts marketing and promotional activities with the Panama City Beach CVB.

The TDC approves and recommends the PCB CVB, Destination Panama City and Mexico Beach budgets/programs of work to the BCC (Aug 25, 2026 agenda for FY2027). The BCC adopts TDC Funds 124-129 in the county budget.

In June 2023 the TDC asked the BCC to raise the rate from 5% to 6%; the motion died for lack of a second. The article reports that a state law change effective July 1, 2023 requires voter approval for future increases.

On Jan 13, 2026 the TDC approved Resolution 2601 giving the Bay County Clerk of Court control of the CVB's bank accounts and financial operations, and hired an independent auditor to review internal controls.

Reggie Johns replaced Clair Pease as chair; Ethan Register vice chair; Will Fleming and Josh Wakstein joined the board. Jeff DeBenedictis became treasurer in January 2026. This is a partial list from news reports, not an official roster.
Griff Griffitts (then a state representative) was selected as Visit PCB president & CEO on March 10, 2026, after Dan Rowe resigned; BCC was to finalize the hire.

context.text: The BCC did not raise the TDT from 5% to 6% after a TDC request; the motion died for lack of a second. Officials from Panama City Beach, Panama City and Mexico Beach backed the increase; some residents opposed it.

context.topic: Beach nourishment money opened to public safety
context.text: The BCC approved letting up to 10% of the beach-renourishment cent go to public safety (sheriff, PCB police, water safety, lifeguards). About $50 million in unused renourishment money was placed in reserves for emergencies. Visit PCB's share rose from 8% to 10% (annual budget $2.6M to $3.2M, per WMBB). Reporting figures do not fully reconcile.
2025 House proposals (HB 1221 amendment, HB 7033) would have redirected bed-tax revenue to property-tax relief or required periodic renewal; local tourism groups opposed them.

Two Visit PCB vice presidents were arrested on grand theft and fraudulent credit-card-use charges (allegations, not convictions). Investigators allege nearly $1 million in charges on one executive's company card from April 2024 to January 2026, of which about $58,000 was documented as business expense. The Clerk took over CVB finances.
Dan Rowe, CVB/TDC president and CEO for 18 years, resigned after being on paid leave since January 13. The TDC accepted the resignation on Feb 2, 2026. No reason was given in the article.

The TDC selected State Rep. Griff Griffitts as president & CEO. Some residents raised conflict-of-interest concerns about his continued legislative service; he said the TDC/CVB do not request state appropriations.

The TDC paused design of the SABRE Event Center / Western Regional Resiliency Center at Publix Sports Park, a facility WMBB described as $60 million, after an outside consultant recommended against the site. About $1.2M had been spent on design. The CVB FY2026 budget had $26,284,629 for the project.
The TDC approved a FY2027 plan reported at more than $54 million.
TDT administration moved from the Clerk of Court to the Bay County Tax Collector.

EDR estimates the value of a 1% countywide levy in Bay at $7,230,874 for SFY 2024-25, from estimated taxable transient rental sales of $723,087,353. This is a statewide estimate method, not a collection figure, and the actual levy is less than countywide.

notes: Fiscal years: county and TDT figures use the county FY (Oct 1-Sep 30, named for the ending year). School district figures use the July-June FY. EDR/DOR state figures use the state FY (July-June).

TDT collections are the Clerk's cash-basis 12-month totals including penalties and interest, taken from the latest September report that covers each year. A later report supersedes an earlier one where they differ (one case: Mexico Beach FY2020).
Mexico Beach and Panama City collections fell sharply in FY2019-FY2020 after Hurricane Michael (Oct 10, 2018). The records show the drop; the reports do not state the cause.
County budget-book FY2025 'actual' TDT tax revenue (Funds 125+127+128 = $45,909,060) exceeds the Clerk's FY2025 PCB tax collections ($36,213,117). The budget book does not explain the difference.
Infrastructure surtax figures on bayhalfcent.com and in Fund 102 cover the county's share only. City projects appear in the GIS layer without costs or with partial costs.

Media reports differ on dates (one says the infrastructure surtax 'first passed in 2015' and would extend to 2034). Official DOR/EDR records show Jan 1, 2017 to Dec 31, 2026, extended to Dec 31, 2036.
Names of people charged in the 2026 CVB case are omitted. Charges are allegations.
gaps: No actual Bay County TDT collections were found for FY2026 beyond July 2026. The full-year September 2026 report was not yet posted.

The Bay County tourist tax ordinance and Tourist Development Plan (the official cent-by-cent allocation) were not retrieved because the county code website couldn't be read by our tools. The 3/1/1-cent split is inferred from FY2024 fund revenue.
No official, complete TDC member roster with seat categories was found online. Only names reported in news coverage are listed.
The ad agency contract value (Luckie) and the PR/media contract values were not found. Only the CVB budget's agency retainer line ($461,135) is available.
TDC/CVB spending by category before FY2024 was not compiled. Older county budget books are on the Budget Office archive page, and older CVB programs of work are on visitpanamacitybeach.com.
Countywide infrastructure-surtax collections (county + cities) are not published separately. EDR's series combines the infrastructure and school surtaxes.

No Citizens Oversight Committee reports or minutes for the infrastructure surtax were found online, and no OPPAGA/independent performance audit for Bay County's 2024 referendum appears on OPPAGA's contracted-reviews page.
City-level surtax spending (Panama City, Lynn Haven, PCB, etc.) was not compiled. City project status comes only from the county GIS layer.
The 2016 ballot named project categories, not a binding project list. The county's First/Last 5 Years schedules show programmed (not necessarily spent) amounts.

Bay District Schools' half-cent page and budget PDFs couldn't be read by our tools. The promised 2018 school project list and per-project school surtax costs were not retrieved. Few school projects could be tied to surtax funding by a source.

School 'Local sales taxes' for FY2016-FY2017 come from the FY2017 Auditor General audit, and FY2018-FY2025 from the district financial statements filed with the Auditor General. No FY2026 figure is available yet.
